text:
Elliot Price: Heads up, I’m seeing terminology drift across the Terraform modules pages + Confluence. Before PR-912 goes much further, can we agree on naming + where things live (docs site vs Confluence)?

Kira Thompson: +1. Right now we have:
- “Redwood Private VPC”
- “Private Deployment (VPC)”
- “Private (VPC) alpha modules”
And the quickstart draft references “installer” without saying redwood-private-installer.

Benji Okafor: From installer side we refer to it as “Redwood Private (VPC)” in UI + config docs. I’d prefer docs site matches that. “Redwood Private VPC” reads like a product sku.

Irene Choi: Agree. Also “Terraform modules (alpha)” should be explicit everywhere. We don’t want customers thinking this is the only supported VPC pattern.

Victor Alvarez: Suggestion:
- Product name: “Redwood Private (VPC)”
- Feature: “VPC Terraform modules (alpha)”
- Module wrapper: “redwood-private-vpc” (actual module name)
- Baseline module: “vpc-baseline”
We should avoid “reference architecture” on the public docs page unless we’re ready to support it like a standard.

Kira Thompson: Re: placement. My current plan was:
Docs site (external):
- Overview + supported topologies
- Module matrix (inputs/outputs at a high level)
- Quickstart (single account)
- Troubleshooting “common failures”
Confluence (internal):
- Deep dive networking rationale
- Ops/runbooks + preflight check details
- CI/integration test notes
Does that match expectations?

Marcus Lin: Security POV: keep threat model + exception rationale internal (Confluence). Public docs can say “secure-by-default” but avoid listing internal risk acceptance details. Also please include a clear “customer-owned responsibility” section for flow logs retention and endpoint policies.

Elliot Price: Makes sense. One more thing: where do we put the “required IAM permissions” doc? That’s typically public.

Irene Choi: Public is fine as long as it’s scoped to *module apply* and not broad account guidance. We should include least-privilege policy snippets and call out “your org may require additional controls.”

Benji Okafor: Also: docs should clearly separate:
1) Terraform deploy (network foundation)
2) Installer deploy (control plane / data plane)
People keep mixing them.

Kira Thompson: Got it. I’ll add a section in quickstart:
- Step 1: Terraform modules
- Step 2: Provide outputs to installer
- Step 3: Run installer preflight
And include explicit “what Terraform produces” vs “what installer consumes”.

Bruno Silva: On wording: “Redwood Private installer” is ok in prose, but first mention should be “redwood-private-installer” with link to repo/docs. After that “Private installer” works.

Elliot Price: Ok, proposal for consistent terminology on docs site:
- “Redwood Private (VPC)” everywhere for the product/deployment type
- “VPC Terraform modules (alpha)” for the module set
- Use module names exactly as in registry/repo (`redwood-private-vpc`, `vpc-baseline`, `vpc-endpoints`, `security-groups-baseline`)
- “Private installer (redwood-private-installer)” on first mention
Everyone ok?

Victor Alvarez: +1. Also please avoid “isolated subnet” vs “private subnet” confusion. In AWS land people interpret differently.
I’d like:
- “public”
- “private (egress)”
- “isolated (no egress)”
And define them once in the overview.

Kira Thompson: Great call. I’ll add a glossary block near the top of the overview.

Marcus Lin: Another small thing: avoid saying “no public egress” unless we also mention you still need endpoints (ECR/S3/STS/etc). We should phrase as “no internet egress” and then list the required PrivateLink/Gateway endpoints.

Benji Okafor: Yes please. We had a pilot fail because they assumed “private” == no endpoints needed. :facepalm:

Elliot Price: Review assignments for PR-912 draft pages:
- Overview + glossary: Victor
- Quickstart: Benji (installer integration correctness) + Bruno (real-world apply steps)
- Troubleshooting: Irene (network gotchas) + Benji (installer errors)
- Security + secure defaults section: Marcus
- Final editorial: Kira + me

Kira Thompson: Works. I’ll also add a “Confluence vs docs site” note to the internal doc plan so we stop duplicating content.

Irene Choi: Can we include a “What’s not supported (alpha)” callout box on every page? Specifically: multi-account TGW topologies are out of scope for alpha, and existing VPC adoption has guardrails.

Elliot Price: Yes. I’ll make it a shared partial so it’s consistent.

Victor Alvarez: One more: in the docs site navigation, please put it under “Private deployment” not “Terraform” top-level. Customers find it by deployment mode.

Kira Thompson: Ack. I’ll move it in the sidebar.

Marcus Lin: When is the security review deadline?

Elliot Price: Aiming EOW for first pass. Marcus, if you can skim by Thursday, we can still make the Monday publish window.

Marcus Lin: Thursday works.

Benji Okafor: I’ll leave comments today/tomorrow. Please tag me if the quickstart includes sample `tfvars` that affect endpoint DNS (private DNS toggles etc).

Kira Thompson: Will do. Thanks all.

Elliot Price: Cool. I’ll summarize decisions in the PR description + link the internal Confluence plan. :thumbsup:

Kira Thompson added a reaction :thumbsup: to Elliot Price’s message
Victor Alvarez added a reaction :white_check_mark: to Elliot Price’s message
